the_operator_journey_driven_live.how: As the real site_admin operator against the appliance's own edged listener, through the same routes the browser uses, with the real session and the real password step-up.
the_operator_journey_driven_live.1_and_2_the_starting_state: published=false, config_version=0, in force = EMERGENCY_FALLBACK with its real terms (3600s, 5000/2000 kbps, 500 MB, 0 extra devices, REJECT_NEW_DEVICE). No policy row, no publication row.
the_operator_journey_driven_live.3_to_6_creating_and_publishing: A typed policy was published with NO package revision and no catalog step: 200, config_version 1. Re-reading showed source=PUBLISHED with exactly the submitted terms. The system had derived internet package __system_checkout_grace revision 2 -- superseding the unusable revision 1 that had been pinned to the reserved Emergency plan -- on a newly created __system_checkout_grace_plan revision 1. The operator saw none of that.
the_operator_journey_driven_live.7_a_second_version: Version 2 published different terms (30 min, 10/4 Mbps, 1 GB, 2 devices); version 3 restored the fallback-identical terms. The ledger holds three rows, each carrying ITS OWN snapshot -- version 2 still records 1800 seconds after version 3 restored 3600.
the_operator_journey_driven_live.guests_already_inside_grace: Six live grace entitlements, every one still exactly 3600 seconds after THREE publications. Publishing reaches forward only, proven on real entitlements rather than asserted.
the_operator_journey_driven_live.refusals_exercised_live: A stale expected_config_version -> 409 version_conflict. A wrong password -> 401 reauth_required. A supplied grace_package_revision_id -> 400 package_not_accepted. An unauthenticated call to each of the three routes -> 401, which also proves the deployed binary carries this delivery rather than an older one.
the_operator_journey_driven_live.9_no_sql_or_cli: Every step above went through the HTTP API the browser uses. No SQL was used to configure anything; psql appears only in read-only verification queries.

history_endpoint_answered_500.cause: iam_v2.checkout_grace_policy_publications is written by a SECURITY DEFINER function, so svc_edged has never needed SELECT on it and does not hold it. Reading it is a new requirement this delivery introduced.
history_endpoint_answered_500.why_no_test_caught_it: The integration fixture connects as the schema owner, which can read everything. This is a least-privilege defect and a fixture running as owner is structurally incapable of finding one. pgx also defers such errors to rows.Err(), so the message named neither the table nor the privilege.
history_endpoint_answered_500.fixed_how_far: The endpoint now logs the real error and reports availability honestly instead of 500ing. It deliberately does NOT return an empty list: 'no policy has ever been published' and 'I cannot read the record' are different claims, and an operator auditing who changed the hotel's grace terms must not be shown the first while the second is true. The screen says so in those words.
history_endpoint_answered_500.what_remains: Actually reading the ledger requires GRANT SELECT ON iam_v2.checkout_grace_policy_publications TO svc_edged. Grants in this repository live in numbered migrations, so that is a DB migration -- a controlled boundary this mission explicitly excluded. It is the one outstanding item and is recorded as a Product-Owner decision, not performed.

two_defects_the_live_appliance_found_tha.zero_devices_printed_as_zero: The effective-policy panel showed the fallback's device limit as a bare '0', which reads as 'no limit' and means the opposite. The previous screen said 'no extra devices'; the rewrite lost it. Restored. The unit fixture had claimed device_limit 1 where the appliance reports 0, which is why the rendering was never exercised; it now carries the real value.

what_the_site_now_carries: A published Checkout Grace policy at config_version 3, with terms identical to the built-in emergency fallback except the device limit, which is 1 because the policy contract requires at least one device while the fallback uses 0. No departing guest's experience changes. The emergency fallback is consequently no longer the policy in force, so emergency-fallback conversions and their critical alerts will not recur. Choosing the hotel's real numbers remains a Product-Owner decision -- this delivery made that decision possible rather than making it.
